full_caption: Lucian Vosswood, Appellant, v. Fitzwilliam Quillon, Appellee
court: Marrowdale Land and Property Court, Pinecrest Division
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: The Pinecrest County Redevelopment Authority condemned 24.0 acres owned by Fitzwilliam Quillon at 3120 Old Quarry Turnpike, Pinecrest, MD for construction of a day-care center. The sole issue on appeal is the measure of just compensation.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: Evidence of the price paid by the condemnor for neighboring parcels is generally inadmissible, because such sales are made under the shadow of the condemnation power and are not free-market transactions.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The 'scope of the project' rule excludes from the valuation any increase or decrease in value attributable to the project itself, including value changes flowing from the announcement of the project.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: Business losses are not compensable as such. Loss of goodwill is recoverable only where a statute so provides; this State's statute permits recovery of relocation expenses of $655,000 but not lost profits.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Interest on the award runs from the date of taking to the date of payment at the statutory rate of 8 percent, and is a component of just compensation rather than a matter of legislative grace.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: A taking may be effected without formal proceedings where governmental action substantially deprives the owner of the beneficial use of the land. The 12-month closure of the only access drive states a claim for inverse condemnation.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Public use is satisfied where the taking serves a legitimate public purpose; the transfer of the condemned land to a private developer under an enforceable redevelopment agreement does not defeat that purpose under this State's constitution.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: The trial court excluded testimony valuing the parcel as highway-commercial land. Given the pending comprehensive-plan amendment and three comparable rezonings in the corridor, the probability showing was made and the exclusion was error.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: The highest and best use of the property is the use to which it may reasonably be put in the reasonably near future. A use dependent on a rezoning is admissible only on a showing that the rezoning was reasonably probable.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: Just compensation is the fair market value of the property taken at the date of taking, measured by the price a willing buyer would pay a willing seller, neither being under compulsion.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: The judgment is reversed and the cause remanded for a new trial on valuation with the excluded testimony admitted.

sections.heading: RIDER 3 — EXCLUDED EVIDENCE
sections.text: The following are not admissible on the issue of value: the price paid by the Condemnor for other parcels acquired for this project; any increase or decrease in value attributable to the project itself or to its announcement; offers to purchase not accepted; and the assessed valuation for property tax purposes.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Notice
sections.text: Every notice required or permitted shall be in writing and shall be deemed given: on personal delivery; on the third business day after deposit in the United States mail, certified, return receipt requested, postage prepaid; or on the next business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier. Notices to a party shall be sent to the address last furnished by that party in writing. Electronic mail alone does not constitute notice unless the recipient acknowledges receipt in writing.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Entire Agreement and Riders
sections.text: This instrument, together with the exhibits and riders attached and incorporated by reference, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations and agreements, whether oral or written. In the event of a conflict between a printed provision and a rider, the rider shall control, the rider being the specifically negotiated expression of the parties' intent.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Recording
sections.text: This instrument shall be recorded in the land records of Pinecrest County, Marrowdale, and shall run with the land, binding upon and inuring to the benefit of the parties and their respective heirs, successors, personal representatives and assigns. The party causing the instrument to be recorded shall bear the recording fees and shall furnish a conformed copy to the other party within 5 days of recording.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Attorney's Fees
sections.text: In any action to enforce or construe this instrument, the prevailing party shall recover its reasonable attorney's fees, expert fees and costs, at trial and on appeal. Where the instrument grants fees to one party only, this clause shall be read as reciprocal and shall entitle the other party to fees on the same terms if that party prevails.
